minutes.headline: Planning Board reorganized, accepted two ANR plans, and heard solar-plus-battery and craft marijuana proposals.
minutes.summary: The board reorganized with a new chair, vice chair and clerk, and welcomed a new member. It accepted a lot-line ANR at Goodrich Street, while an Electric Avenue ANR raised a pump station setback question needing more information. Most time went to a pre-submission battery and solar proposal on Chase Road, craft marijuana cultivator rules and prohibition ballot questions, and the draft permitting guidebook.

public_comment.topic: Objected to solar and battery expansion: buffering, trails, pilot agreement, lithium battery safety, grid capacity, alternative sites.
Supports prohibition of marijuana uses; concerned about gray areas and abutters.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board accepted the ANR plan for 388 and 390 Goodrich Street by vote.
An ANR plan on Electric Avenue was held until the applicant adds the pump station structure dimension.
The board will prepare a draft letter and rationale on five marijuana prohibition questions for a December 11th discussion with the Board of Selectmen.
A pre-submission solar and battery proposal on Chase Road drew a resident objection and a question on whether the existing solar tax agreement would reopen.
The board named members as Green Communities task force liaison and Charter Review Committee representative, and the planner will bring a draft marijuana framework to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The marijuana prohibition questions and the Chase Road battery and solar proposal bear on land use near homes and trails, and on a tax agreement that sets what the solar owner pays the town.
Residents may be asked to vote on the marijuana prohibition questions, so the rules drafted now will shape what they see on the ballot.
watch_next: December 11th discussion with the Board of Selectmen on the five prohibition questions, and the board's draft letter and rationale before it.
The planner's draft marijuana framework and clarifications at the next meeting, and the permitting guidebook revisions due back on the 10th.
